source_ref: Wernike K & Beer M, Vet Microbiol 290:109985
evidence_quote: infectious virus could be isolated only in just under half of the attempts (43.33%)
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). n=40 labs from 10 countries; 18 attempted virus isolation. Cell lines bovine (BEL, EKANAEP, KLu-R, KOP-R, MDBK, primary calf testicular) and ovine (SFT). Serum/medium NOT disclosed. Panel included pestivirus-negative samples (all correctly negative). Sensitivity 43.33% (BDV=positive, doubtful=negative) or 46.67% (doubtful=positive); specificity 100%. Authors: virus isolation 'time-consuming and insensitive', not suitable for routine eradication testing.

source_ref: Leung VKY et al., J Clin Virol 142:104907 (second EQA)
evidence_quote: 6/19 laboratories obtained 15/15 correct results in 2016 compared to 11/19 in 2019
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). n=19 NICs (14 WPR, 5 SEAR). EQA samples diluted in serum-free DMEM; trypsin <1-5+ ug/ml; maintenance FBS not stated (hence serum_disclosed=partial). Controls: negative used by 12/19, positive by 11/19 → 7/19 labs ran NO negative control. CPE assessed by 18/19. False positives: 1 lab positive on each of 2 negative samples. Improvement 2016→2019 attributed to follow-up + in-country training + corrective measures (NOT serum/threshold); authors recommend standardization of reagents/protocols.

source_ref: Reading PC et al., J Clin Virol 97:54-58 (first EQA, 2016)
discordance_metric: labs correctly isolating each low-titre sample
evidence_quote: The lowest percentage of laboratories reported influenza virus isolation from EQA samples VIP-2016-12 (52% correct), VIP-2106-05 (62% correct) and VIP-2016-11 (62% correct)
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read, accepted manuscript). n=21 NICs, MDCK/MDCK-SIAT1. Controls: negative used by 16/21, positive by 12/21 → 5/21 labs ran NO negative control. CPE assessed by 19/21 as first growth readout. Serum-free DMEM dilution of EQA samples; trypsin 0.2-125 ug/ml; maintenance FBS not stated (serum_disclosed=partial). False positives: 2/21 reported positive on 1/3 negative samples. Authors recommend standard-protocol harmonization. Note: source manuscript itself prints 'VIP-2106-05' (likely typo for VIP-2016-05); transcribed as printed.

source_ref: Goodell CK et al., Can J Vet Res 80:12-20
discordance_metric: virus-isolation detection-dose-50 (DD50) range across 7 VI assays
evidence_quote: The analysis identified marked differences in rRT-PCR and VI performance and a general lack of reproducibility among the participating laboratories
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). n=8 labs, 13 rRT-PCR + 7 VI assays, 180 randomized OF samples (10 reps x 8 dilutions x 2 subtypes + 20 negatives). VI: 1 assay reported a single false-positive among 20 negatives; VI generally unsuccessful at dilutions >10^-4. Appendix discloses serum-free MEM/3X/Tr for the top 2 VI assays only (serum_disclosed=partial). Authors: variability in equipment/conditions/reagents/protocols precluded identifying specific causal variables; some labs declined to share protocols (IP).

source_ref: Pérez-Ramírez E et al., PLoS One 15:e0239478 (RVF, MediLabSecure)
evidence_quote: The performance was good in the molecular panel with 70.6% of participants reporting 100% correct results
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). Secondary tier: molecular + serology EQA, NOT virus isolation (viruses inactivated with beta-propiolactone, spiked into serum/blood/liver/spleen). n=17 labs. All labs given IDENTICAL protocols/reagents/kits (shared template) → high concordance is template-following. One lab (#17) misidentified 70% of samples (1 FP + 6 FN); one lab using a DIFFERENT commercial kit got 3 FN. p3_inheritance_flag=yes: positive reference = inactivated culture-derived virus stocks (MP12 vaccine strain, Namibia 2010).

source_ref: Yu S et al., Viruses 16:1512 (anti-AAV9 MN inter-lab)
evidence_quote: The titers of the blind samples showed excellent reproducibility within and among laboratories, with a %GCV of 18-59% and 23-46%
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). Secondary tier (neutralization titer, n=3 labs: sponsor + CRO + hospital). Method standardized then TRANSFERRED with key materials provided before blind comparison → high concordance is template-following, not independent discovery. Serum disclosed: DMEM+10% FBS (D10) for cells; 0.1% BSA assay buffer. Endpoint choice matters: IC50 (23-46% GCV) less variable than cut-off titer (42-97%). Authors: accuracy 'achieved by strictly implementing SOPs, standardizing key materials, QC criteria and modeling the IC50 endpoint'.

source_ref: Wernike K & Beer M, BMC Vet Res 18:168 (BVDV serology trial)
evidence_quote: These 4 milk samples tested negative in 43.6%, 50.9%, 3.6% and 56.4%, respectively, of all investigations
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). Secondary tier: serology ring trial (n=51 labs + 3 kit manufacturers, 9 commercial + 1 in-house ELISA + neutralization). Discordance driven by ELISA kit choice and sample-incubation protocol (short vs over-night), NOT by inter-lab replication of a single fixed assay. Negative samples mostly correct (specificity 99.49%). Pattern: kit/protocol drift, not rater drift. This is the paper mislabelled as wernike2024; it is the 2022 serology trial, distinct from the 2024 isolation trial (P7-001).

source_ref: Olesen AS et al., Pathogens 11:325 (ASFV multi-lab)
discordance_metric: virus-infectivity detection probability across 6 assays (3 labs)
evidence_quote: For virus infectivity assays in cells, the probability of detecting infectious ASFV varied from 0.68 to 0.90
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). First-class Isolation row: virus infectivity (Isolation/titration, HAD50/TCID50) in cells, n=3 national reference labs (DTU, FLI, WBVR), 80 samples, 6 ASFV strains. Detection probability 0.68-0.90 across 6 infectivity assays vs qPCR 0.96-1.0; ICC between infectivity assays 0.80-0.94. Serum disclosed (5-10% FCS, varies by lab/cell). Authors: primary cells (PAMs) most sensitive but batch-to-batch variation; operator experience more crucial for infectivity (manual microscope reading) than qPCR. Readout is HAD/IPMA/IFA, not CPE.

source_ref: Wernike K & Beer M, Vet Microbiol 239:108452 (German BVDV)
discordance_metric: antibody ELISA kits needing adjustment; milk false-negatives by incubation protocol
discordance_value: 4 of 9 ELISA kits; milk S-7/S-9 false-negative in up to 6 cases (short vs overnight incubation)
evidence_quote: for four of the applied nine antibody ELISA kits adjustments are recommended
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). Secondary tier: antigen ELISA + RT-PCR + serology, NOT virus isolation. n=34 German regional labs + 5 kit manufacturers. Virological panel reliable (antigen ELISA 100%, RT-PCR 98.73%). Serology: 4 of 9 antibody ELISA kits needed adjustment; one serum + both milk samples false-negative by some kits; milk S-7/S-9 false-negative in up to 6 cases, tracking short-vs-overnight incubation protocol. Same kit/protocol-drift pattern as P7-007.

source_ref: Brangel P et al., Viruses 16:1936 (SARS-CoV-2 antigenicity 15 labs)
discordance_metric: titre magnitude spread between assay types (live MN vs pseudovirus)
discordance_value: 3.2 log2 units (~9-fold) mean difference; fold drops consistent (RMSD 0.59)
evidence_quote: Titre magnitudes were seen to vary largely even for labs within the same assay group
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). Secondary tier: 15-lab neutralization comparison using common reagents (NIBSC standard). Nuanced: relative fold-drops consistent (RMSD 0.59) but ABSOLUTE titre magnitude varies ~3.2 log2 (~9-fold) between live MN (lowest) and pseudovirus (highest), even within same assay group. Shows 'concordance' depends on endpoint: relative antigenic distance reproducible, absolute titre not. harmonization=yes (common reagents supplied).

source_ref: Onyilagha C et al., Front Vet Sci 13:1874382 (CSF/ASF Americas)
discordance_metric: CSF serology accuracy vs ASF serology vs molecular
discordance_value: CSF serology 35.7%; ASF serology 80%; CSF molecular 85.7%; ASF molecular 100%
evidence_quote: only 35.7% accurately identified the CSF-positive serum samples
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). Secondary tier: molecular + serology EQA, NOT virus isolation (inactivated viruses). n=16 labs from 11 countries. Molecular: ASF 100%, CSF 85.7%. Serology: ASF 80%, CSF only 35.7%. p3_inheritance_flag=yes: positive reference = inactivated culture-derived virus (ASFV in PPLs, CSFV in PK-15). CSF serology discordance is the headline.

source_ref: Gourlaouen M et al., PLoS Negl Trop Dis 14:e0008010 (rabies, Sub-Saharan Africa)
discordance_metric: DFA (microscopic FA) concordance vs RT-PCR concordance
evidence_quote: results showed a higher proficiency in applying the molecular test compared to the DFA test
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). Secondary tier, but key for OB080/OB081: DFA = human-microscope-read fluorescent-antibody (visual readout) underperforms molecular RT-PCR (87.69% vs 98.2% concordance). Isolates the VISUAL-READOUT underperformance separate from cell-culture propagation: same asymmetry OB080 reports, but the 'microscopy judgment' component. n=13 labs DFA, 11 RT-PCR, 10 both. NOT virus isolation/CPE.

source_ref: Clavijo A et al., PLoS Negl Trop Dis 11:e0005427 (rabies, LAC)
discordance_value: large variability in throughput/equipment/protocols (no single discordance rate in abstract)
evidence_quote: Answers to the online questionnaire indicated large variability in the laboratories throughput, equipment used, protocols availability, quality control standards
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read of abstract+front; results discordance numbers need Methods/Results re-read). Secondary tier: DFA proficiency, n=23 labs. Documents heterogeneity in DFA practice (no standardized protocol in region) rather than a single scored discordance rate. Supports the 'visual readout is unstandardized across labs' premise behind DFA underperformance in P7-012.

Molecular proficiency near-perfect at low dilution, degrades only at extreme 1:1e6. ELISA 100% concordance. This is a BLINDED molecular/serology panel with high concordance — supports the molecular-side reproducibility (detection) that OB080 contrasts against.

source_ref: Dill V et al., Vet Microbiol 203:62-67 (FMD, Germany)
discordance_value: RT-PCR reliable to 10^-4 (1 exception); LFD 1:81 all 8 labs; ELISA specificity >99%
evidence_quote: With only one exception, all laboratories reliably detected viral RNA with two real-time RT-PCR assays
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). Secondary tier: RT-PCR + LFD antigen + serology, NOT isolation. n=20 labs. Molecular robust; LFD (pen-side) and ELISA consistent. Predecessor to Keck 2022 (same group); notes earlier German FMD ring trials used non-blinded self-made dilutions.

source_ref: Fischer M et al., PLoS One 8:e58372 (lyssavirus molecular)

coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). Secondary tier: lyssavirus RT-PCR ring trial, n=16 labs. Molecular detection robust overall; discordance concentrated in labs/applying single assay vs >1 assay. Supports molecular detection reproducibility with a caveat (redundancy reduces discordance).

source_ref: Gigante CM et al., PLoS One 13:e0197074 (LN34 lyssavirus multi-site)
discordance_value: LN34 sensitivity/specificity vs gold-standard DFA (see Results for exact %s)
evidence_quote: no quote (abstract notes LN34 is a strong candidate; DFA requires skilled technician + fluorescence microscope)
coder_note: VERIFIED (front matter + abstract read; Results concordance %s need re-read). Secondary tier: multi-site LN34 pan-lyssavirus RT-PCR vs DFA gold standard. Molecular detection candidate; DFA characterized as requiring 'skilled technician + fluorescence microscope'. Supports the P7-012 finding that the microscopic DFA readout carries operator skill burden.

source_ref: Ferris NP et al., Vet Microbiol 117:130-140 (FMD isolation, Europe)
discordance_value: variable: high in 1 lab, moderate in 2, low in 2; RT-PCR comparable across labs
evidence_quote: the sensitivity of cell cultures was variable from high in one laboratory, moderate in two and low in two others
coder_note: VERIFIED (full text read). FIRST-CLASS Isolation row for OB080. n=5 European reference labs, 20 coded samples each, EXPLICITLY BLIND ('coded randomly from 1 to 100 to ensure testing was performed blind'). RT-PCR: all universal assays specific, detected all 4 serotypes, comparable across labs. VI (cell culture): sensitivity 'differed considerably between laboratories'; even the same IB-RS-2 cell line gave lab-order sensitivity B>C>E>D>A; BTY primary cells best, BHK worst. Serum disclosed partially (MEM 2% FCS for Lab C; serum-free maintenance elsewhere; Lab E 10% FCS growth). Blind, yet cell-culture endpoint still underperforms molecular — answers the blinding question for the FMD panel.
